_comment: Sweep-agent allowlist. The agent runs `claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits`, so Edit/Write are
auto-accepted but EVERY Bash command must match a rule — there is no human to prompt, so a miss is an
immediate denial. Run 20260816-165919 lost 13 of 61 turns (~17%) to denials, and NONE of them were
about a domain: the SEC entries below were never even exercised, because the agent reached EDGAR
through node scripts using the app's own httpGet. The denials were about SHAPE.
Rules are prefix matches over the command string; a compound command is checked per segment, so
allowing `cd` is what makes `cd /path && git log` work at all.
DENY still wins over everything here (see .claude/settings.json: git commit/reset/checkout/branch/
push/tag, rm, npm install, npx). That is why there is no bare `VAR=*` rule: `FOO=1 git commit` does
not start with `git commit`, so a blanket env-prefix rule would silently punch through the deny list.
Env-prefix rules are therefore bound to `node`, which is already fully allowed on its own.
Read-only diagnostics only. Nothing here writes to the repo, deploys, or touches .env. Writing a
scratch script is done with the Write tool (auto-accepted) and then `node file.js` — NOT with a
`cat > file <<EOF` heredoc, which is a shell write primitive and is deliberately not allowed.
